title: CSV export on the reports page
constraints: Exports must not hold more than 1,000 rows in memory at once

context.summary: The reports page lists filtered report rows from Postgres through the Reports API. Today there is no export: users copy the table by hand. The feature adds a streaming CSV endpoint and an Export button that downloads the current filter's rows.

steps.title: CSV row formatter
steps.intent: A pure function that turns one report row into one RFC 4180 CSV line: quotes fields containing commas, quotes or newlines, doubles inner quotes, and renders null as an empty field. Everything downstream streams through it, so it is proven first and alone.

steps.title: Cursor-paged report query
steps.intent: Add a query that yields report rows for a filter in pages of at most 1,000, ordered by id, so the exporter can stream without loading the whole result. Reuses the existing filter-to-SQL builder.

risk.note: ordering by id must match the index the page already uses or large exports slow down

steps.title: CSV stream
steps.intent: Compose the formatter and the paged query into a readable stream: header line first, then one formatted line per row, page by page. Memory stays bounded by one page, which is the constraint the spec sets.

risk.note: backpressure: Readable.from honours it, a hand-rolled push stream would not

steps.diff_sketch:
- buffer all rows, then join
+ Readable.from(async generator): header, then one line per row, one page in memory

infographic.title: Peak memory for a 50,000-row export (MB, from the streaming research)

steps.title: Export button
steps.intent: Add an Export CSV button to the reports page toolbar, disabled while the table is empty, that opens the export URL for the current filter in a new tab. The URL builder is tested; the endpoint arrives in T5.

steps.title: GET /api/reports/export
steps.intent: A route that validates the filter query, sets text/csv and a Content-Disposition attachment header, and pipes the CSV stream to the response. Reuses the existing filter parser and auth guard of the Reports API.

risk.note: an invalid filter must return 400, not an empty CSV; the parser already throws, the route must map it

steps.title: Wire the button into the page
steps.intent: Render ExportButton in the reports toolbar with the live filter and row count, so the download reflects what the user sees. Integration step: it touches the page and depends on both the button and the endpoint.

steps.title: Full verification
steps.intent: Run the whole suite, the type-check, lint and the build, and prove the memory constraint end to end with a 50,000-row export under the test harness's heap limit.

green.sketch: No production change expected; if the test fails, the page size in T2 or the generator in T3 is the fix.
